purpose: Discriminate update-admission protection from recognition-validity protection in an online familiarity loop under near-confuser unknowns and mild known-class appearance shift.
interpretation: Evidence-gated update admission prevented self-labeled unknowns from contaminating persistent prototype updates in this proxy.
Update admission alone did not solve recognition: near-confuser false familiarity remained high.
Adding an independent imperfect context/semantic validity gate sharply reduced false familiarity, at the cost of lower known fast-path acceptance.
Update-admission and recognition-validity are therefore distinct control surfaces and should remain independently ablatable.
limitations: 2D Gaussian proxy; not real Retina embeddings or project hardware.
The context mismatch signal is synthetic and intentionally informative; it does not prove a specific FRANK context gate.
No claim of optimal thresholds or conformal guarantees.
promotion_status: NOT_PROMOTABLE; informs BASE/Harness test design only
